newsitem.title: USA: U.S., two Koreas fail to arrange crucial meeting.
newsitem.headline: U.S., two Koreas fail to arrange crucial meeting.

text.p: U.S., South and North Korean representatives held more informal talks on Sunday but again failed to arrange a twice-delayed meeting at which Pyongyang would say if it would join in landmark peace talks.
The aim was to try to hold the meeting on Monday but after three hours of discussion in New York, a U.S. spokesman said the three sides failed to reach a conclusion.
"There is still no meeting scheduled," the spokesman told Reuters, adding: "That's all I'm getting tonight."
He did not say if the South Korean delegation, which planned to leave New York on Friday night, would stay on. A South Korean spokesman could not be reached.

There were unconfirmed reports that senior negotiators from North and South Korea were at the talks. But the U.S. spokesman said the American side was represented by a lower- level official, not chief negotiator Charles Kartman, who was reported to be in Washington.
"We are not having a heads of delegation meeting at which North Korea would respond to the U.S. and South Korean proposal" for four party peace talks, the U.S. spokesman insisted.
"The United States is represented here only at the working level" in the person of Mark Minton, head of the State Department's Korea desk, he said.

The three delegations, headed by senior negotiators, met last Wednesday in formal session to hear the North's response to a year-old U.S.-South Korean proposal for four-party peace talks that would finally close the books on the 1950-53 Korean War by replacing the fraying armistice with a peace treaty.
Although the discussions were inconclusive, negotiators reported "encouraging progress" and agreed to resume meetings on Friday.
But the North Koreans, saying they awaited instructions from Pyongyang, never showed for Friday's meeting, which was re-set for Saturday. The North Koreans again failed to appear on Saturday.
The three sides maintained "contacts" all weekend in hopes of getting the formal chief negotiators' meeting back on track.
Peace talks, if accepted by Pyongyang's Stalinist regime, may not begin until June or July. China would be the fourth participant along with the United States, South Korea and North Korea.
